what: NVR builds houses in the eastern United States under the Ryan Homes, NVHomes and Heartland Homes names, and it finances many of the buyers through its own mortgage arm.
customers: First-time and move-up buyers in the Mid-Atlantic, Southeast and Midwest.
money: houses built and sold under three brands
mortgages originated for its own buyers and sold on
moat: A land strategy no other builder matches: NVR options lots instead of buying land outright, so when the market turns it walks away from the option rather than sitting on expensive land. That keeps its return on capital far above the industry's.
risks: Mortgage rates decide how many houses sell, and the company has no control over them
Buyer incentives have been rising, which comes straight out of the margin
Concentrated in the eastern United States rather than spread across the country
opportunities: 15 times earnings and $818M of free cash flow, with $2.0B of cash against only $144M of debt
The option model means a downturn costs far less than it does for builders holding land
Buying back shares steadily, which is why earnings per share hold up even when volumes do not
watch: New orders and the cancellation rate, which move before revenue does.
